fit: combined Parkinson diet program and apathy ascertainment
assessment: The qualitative report describes pre-existing apathy as a barrier. The same trial registered Starkstein apathy and reported baseline prevalence but no post-intervention arm estimates. No analyzed chervil intake.

fit: personalized plant-rich diet and time-restricted eating with apathy outcomes
assessment: Apathy rating changed 13.65 to 9.0 with the program and 13.05 to 13.6 with control. The time-by-group and post-treatment comparisons are distinct, with conflicting post-treatment statements. There is no chervil-specific exposure or estimate.

fit: encapsulated ginger and gastrointestinal symptom scores outside Parkinson disease
assessment: Gastric half-emptying was faster after capsules. The measured gastrointestinal symptoms gave inconclusive contrasts in 11 people. This does not directly address grated ginger or Parkinson pain severity.
